title: Short Stuff: Parachute Emergency!
summary: Short Stuff episode on parachute emergencies. The hosts discuss the rarity of parachute malfunctions (about one in a thousand jumps, per USPA member Ron Bell with thirteen thousand jumps), the two main partial malfunctions (line twist and line over), total malfunctions and the reserve parachute, the rule 'when in doubt, whip it out,' and automatic activation devices (AADs) that deploy the reserve if a jumper is falling below 1,000 feet at speeds of at least 78 mph. They cite skydiving fatality figures (32 deaths in 2000 out of 2.7 million jumps, and 11 deaths in a later count out of 2.8 million) and survival stories including Victoria Sillers, Michael Holmes, and Vesna Vulovich. The episode includes an ad break for a sponsor read.
topics: when in doubt whip it out

segments.title: Opening banter on skydiving experiences
segments.summary: Hosts chat about whether they have skydived, Josh's tandem jump experience, and their hesitation about trying it.

segments.title: Parachute malfunction odds
segments.summary: Ron Bell, a USPA member with thirteen thousand jumps and fourteen malfunctions, says about one in a thousand jumps has a malfunction. The hosts note a malfunction does not automatically mean death.

segments.title: Terminal velocity and partial malfunctions
segments.summary: Terminal velocity is about 120 mph after about twelve seconds of falling. The hosts describe partial malfunctions and the line twist, which can be undone by twisting the other way.

segments.title: Line over malfunction
segments.summary: A line over occurs when a line crosses over the canopy, so the parachute works but not as it should. This can be a serious problem when the main parachute fails to open.

segments.title: Total malfunction and reserve parachute
segments.summary: If the main parachute does not deploy, the jumper uses the reserve. Reserve packing must be done by certified riggers, and a main that does not deploy can be better than one tangled with the reserve. Hosts cite Bell's advice, 'when in doubt, whip it out.'
topics: when in doubt whip it out

segments.title: Automatic activation devices
segments.summary: Modern automatic activation devices (AADs) use sensors to deploy the reserve if a jumper is falling below 1,000 feet at at least 78 mph. The hosts also discuss a naked skydiver anecdote.

segments.title: Skydiving fatality statistics and survival stories
segments.summary: Fatality rates are very low: 32 deaths in 2000 out of 2.7 million jumps and 11 out of 2.8 million in a later count. The hosts cite survivors Victoria Sillers, Michael Holmes, and Vesna Vulovich.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts close the short episode with a joke about whipping it out and sign off.
